A person walking along a straight road observes that at two consecutive
kilometer-stones the angles of elevation of a hill in front of him are 30° and 60° respectively. What is the height of the hill?
When the angle of depression from the sun was 30°, the length of the shadow of a tree was 6√3 m. What will be the length of the shadow of the tree when the angle of depression from the sun is 60°?
solutionText: Height of tree = shadow × tan 30° = 6√3 × 1/√3 = 6 m. When the angle is 60°, shadow = height/tan 60° = 6/√3 = 2√3 m. Therefore the answer is 2√3 m. Link: https://youtu.be/UNklq50VFbY?t=439
